name: Question 5
problem:
Write the following first-order linear ODE in standard form.

$$
\frac{dy}{dx}+{y}^{2}{(\operatorname{cos}⁡x)}^{2}={(1-y\operatorname{cos}⁡x)}^{2}\,.
$$
worked_solution:
A first-order linear ODE is in standard form if it is written as

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+P(x)y=Q(x).
$$

Converting the given equation to standard form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{dy}{dx}+{y}^{2}{(\operatorname{cos}⁡x)}^{2} & ={(1-y\operatorname{cos}⁡x)}^{2} \\ \frac{dy}{dx}+{y}^{2}{(\operatorname{cos}⁡x)}^{2} & =1+{y}^{2}{(\operatorname{cos}⁡x)}^{2}-2y\operatorname{cos}⁡x \\ \frac{dy}{dx} & =1-2y\operatorname{cos}⁡x \\ \frac{dy}{dx}+{{2\operatorname{cos}⁡x}_{⏟}}_{P(x)}\,y & ={{1}_{⏟}}_{Q(x)}\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the equation is written in standard form with $P(x)=2\operatorname{cos}⁡x$ and $Q(x)=1.$

Question 5
?

Write the following first-order linear ODE in standard form. dydx+y2(cos⁡x)2=(1−ycos⁡x)2.

a
dydx=1
b
dydx+y(cos⁡x)2=(1−cos⁡x)2
c
dydx+ycos⁡x=1−cos⁡x
d
dydx+4ycos⁡x=1
e
dydx+2ycos⁡x=1
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

A first-order linear ODE is in standard form if it is written as dydx+P(x)y=Q(x).

Converting the given equation to standard form, we have

dydx+y2(cos⁡x)2=(1−ycos⁡x)2dydx+y2(cos⁡x)2=1+y2(cos⁡x)2−2ycos⁡xdydx=1−2ycos⁡xdydx+2cos⁡x⏟P(x)y=1⏟Q(x).

Now, the equation is written in standard form with P(x)=2cos⁡x and Q(x)=1.
